title: Introduce lightweight fallback proxy and region shard pruning to reduce hotpath contention
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The smart routing hotpath is contending on shared policy state and fallback evaluation locks during regional fanout under bursty traffic. This causes p99 request tail latency to spike and increases GC/CPU pressure on the router process. Goal: introduce a lightweight fallback proxy (an event-driven, single-responsibility actor per region shard) to (1) remove fallback evaluation from the routing hotpath, (2) enable shard pruning for quiet regions to reduce timers/work, and (3) make fallback decisions cacheable and observable without inflating router locks. This ticket implements the proxy, the shard lifecycle manager, and the plumbing to migrate a subset of traffic to the new path for canary testing.
acceptance_criteria: Can route >= 25% of production traffic to fallback proxy for two regions in canary without increased error rate
Router p99 token eval path latency reduced by >= 30% in lab benchmarks when proxy is enabled
No increase in request failure rate or incorrect fallback decisions during 48h canary
Proxy includes metrics for decisions, cache hit/miss, and per-shard queue depth exposed to Console
Automated integration tests for shard lifecycle, graceful drain, and replay on proxy restart
technical_notes: Design: add fallback-proxy process written in Go using same RPC contract as router but with an event-driven worker per shard (shard = region+model-hint).
State: proxy keeps ephemeral LRU decision cache (TTL 30s) and durable shard metadata in existing routing-config store (no new DB).
Shard pruning: track last-active timestamp and reduce polling/heartbeat to one/min for quiet shards, full restore on demand.
Trade-offs: extra network hop for fallback decisions (+~0.5ms median) vs. elimination of lock contention and tail latency reduction.

Dependency changes: upgrade routing-core 0.9.2 -> 1.1.0 (adds compact shard descriptor API), require minor callsite adapters in router. Update grpc-go to 1.56.0 to get improved stream window handling.
HA/Recovery: proxy supports leader election within a region via consul/etcd lease; on leader failover, in-flight requests are retried by router with exponential backoff and idempotency key.
Observability: add fallback.decision_latency, fallback.cache_hit, fallback.proxy_errors to Console; trace span for fallback.proxy_call.
Security: proxy runs in same network zone as the router and uses mTLS; KMS keys unchanged (no new customer data stored).
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Spike complete. Microbenchmarks show lock contention account for ~40% of p99 tail in router when regional fanout > 50 reqs/s.
2025-02-15: Implemented initial proxy skeleton and shard manager; can start/stop shard worker. Local integration tests added.
2025-02-19: Upgraded routing-core to v1.1.0 in branch eng/ENG-34567/proxy, fixed callsite adapters. CI failing on grpc-go upgrade timeouts—investigating window sizes.
2025-02-22: Added LRU cache and TTL eviction. End-to-end lab runs show median +0.6ms added by proxy, p99 router hotpath reduced by ~36% in synthetic workload.
2025-02-25: Canary plan drafted with SRE: two low-traffic regions (eu-west and ap-south) for 24-48h, rollback on >1.5x error rate or >10% latency regression in user-initiated routes.
